A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAVIS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original VIS/VPS benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative analyses in Tables 1–3 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds expanded ablations, long-video evaluation, inference-time measurements and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The CAIT feature extraction, context-aware attention, Hungarian alignment and PCC construction remain unchanged. V2 tests alternative filters and attention values but retains the original proposed configuration; implementation clarifications do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on the 71 additional long videos from YouTube-VIS 2022, testing extended tracking with appearing and disappearing objects (Appendix A.3, Table 6). The original YouTube-VIS 2019/2021, OVIS and VIPSeg coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds CAROQ comparisons with ResNet-50 and Swin-L, plus VISAGE with ResNet-50, across the three retained VIS benchmarks. These methods were absent from v1 Table 1. Existing VIS comparators and the VPS comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluation design. New main-text ablations use the standard training settings, including three segmenter frames and 160k tracker iterations, while the earlier reduced ablations remain in Table 5. It also adds a joint filter-size/frame-count design, a 71-video long-video protocol and inference timing under matched ResNet-50/RTX2080Ti conditions.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining v1 Table 3 as appendix Table 5, v2 adds component ablations measuring both segmenter and tracker outcomes, joint filter/frame sensitivity, max/median filter comparisons and an attention-value ablation (Table 4). New qualitative studies examine mask errors, embedding-related tracking failures, oversized filters and rapidly changing context (Figures 4 and 6–8).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared VIS/VPS scores and the original ablation values are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial ablation results, long-video AP of 38.6 and inference time of 85.6 ms. Added VISAGE results exceed CAVIS on ResNet-50 YTVIS21 AP, 51.6 versus 50.5. New ablation settings preclude simple before/after performance claims. V2 also reports 28.7 for the two-frame, 11x11 filter in Table 4, while retained Table 5 gives 28.9.

T1.justification: Equation (4) removes the negative-log ratio and its asserted equality to the retained double-sum contrastive expression. These expressions are not generally equivalent with multiple positive embeddings, so this removes a mathematical inconsistency. The remaining mathematical constructions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same CAIT/PCC contributions, cross-frame consistency claims and claimed leading VIS/VPS performance, particularly on OVIS. Removing the numbered contribution recap does not remove these claims; acknowledging VISAGE as inspiration changes positioning without redefining the proposed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 newly acknowledges dependence on segmentation-mask accuracy in Appendix A.1. It also explains the attention-value choice, discusses oversized context windows around small objects and interprets the measured latency–accuracy tradeoff. These qualify and extend the existing explanation of contextual tracking.

D1.justification: V2 specifies spatial averaging, channel-wise concatenation and use of the last pixel-decoder feature maps, and documents hardware/backbone conditions for the timing comparison. The core optimizer, initialization, global training schedule, loss weights and project-page access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds VISAGE as a cited work and explicitly credits it as inspiration for PCC. It expands discussion of the already-cited CAROQ, contrasting its full-context memory representation with CAVIS's local surrounding features. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds the CAVIS title prefix, removes the introductory contribution list, revises PCC and related-work explanations, and reorganizes the ablation discussion and appendix studies. Most original prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially redistributing text, equations and displays. V2 adds a notation table, restructures the main ablation table, relocates the original ablations to the appendix, and adds long-video/timing tables and four qualitative figures. Original qualitative panels are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation and transparency through expanded component controls, long-video evaluation, measured latency and an explicit mask-error limitation. These improve support for the unchanged method. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 7 implies a 7.4-point OVIS improvement over DVIS, while the accompanying discussion states 7.6, and the two-frame 11x11 filter result differs between Tables 4 and 5.
